data.name: settings.linkly.sop.manual.steps
data.value: 1. Use this only when ANZ Worldline has configured the terminal for standalone operation. Standalone sales are not sent from HB POS. 2. On the terminal home screen, key in the purchase amount and press OK or ENTER. 3. Ask the customer to tap, insert, or swipe, then follow any account and PIN prompts.

data.name: settings.linkly.sop.ip.title
data.value: Switch HB POS to a Linkly EFT-Client IP connection

data.name: settings.linkly.sop.ip.steps
data.value: 1. Confirm ANZ Worldline or your installer has configured the terminal for integrated operation. PC settings alone do not convert a standalone terminal. 2. On the Windows PC, open Linkly Configuration Wizard. Set the Pinpad port to match the terminal connection. Select TCPIP only when the terminal itself connects over IP, then apply the change. 3. In HB POS, select Local IP / Port and clear Use Linkly Cloud. 4. Set Host to the PC running Linkly EFT-Client. Use 127.0.0.1 on the same PC. The default EFT-Client TCP port is 2011. 5. From another POS PC, use the EFT-Client PC's LAN IP. Allow TCP 2011 through Windows Firewall and add the POS IP to the EFT-Client access list if that list is enabled. 6. Click Test Linkly. After it succeeds, click Enable Linkly.

data.value: The internet works and a reference server answers quickly, but this machine cannot reach the POS server in time. Check firewall and antivirus rules for outbound port 443, any router or provider filtering, and try another network. Other devices on the same network working does not rule out a rule that only affects this machine.

data.name: settings.network.finding.certificateRootMissing.message
data.value: The POS server's certificate chains up to Let's Encrypt's ISRG Root X1, which is missing from this machine's trusted roots. Windows then waits on the network to look it up, so the secure connection stalls. You can install that root certificate below. It is Let's Encrypt's own public root, checked against a built-in fingerprint first.

data.name: settings.network.finding.certificateCheckSlow.title

data.name: settings.network.finding.certificateCheckSlow.message
data.value: The secure connection itself is quick, but Windows spends seconds looking up certificate or revocation information online. Allow this machine to reach Windows Update and Let's Encrypt (lencr.org), or ask your network administrator.

data.name: settings.network.finding.httpsIntercepted.title

data.name: settings.network.finding.httpsIntercepted.message

An antivirus 'HTTPS scanning' or web-protection feature, a proxy, or a firewall appliance is inspecting HTTPS and slowing or breaking it. Exclude hotbargain.vip and HB POS from HTTPS scanning, or turn that feature off for them.

data.name: settings.network.fix.installTrustedRoots

data.name: settings.network.confirm.roots

data.name: settings.network.finding.serverPathLossy.title
data.value: Connections to the POS server are unreliable

data.name: settings.network.finding.serverPathLossy.message
data.value: Some new connections to the POS server stall or fail, while the same machine reaches a reference server every time. The problem is on the route to the server (your internet provider or something along the way). Run 'pathping -n hotbargain.vip' to see where packets are lost, try another network, and tell your provider where the loss starts. Once a connection is open the POS keeps using it, so the delays mostly appear when it has to reconnect.

Check the router for connection limits or 'DoS / SYN flood protection' settings, and the antivirus for network-attack protection.
